webster.text: To kick; to drive back or away, as with the foot.

more.text: To reject with disdain; to scorn to receive or accept.
To kick or toss up the heels.

example.quote: Those who are not so well informed will spurn at the government.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 3, Virginia Convention, June 12, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
